scope.model: Neutral authored reconstruction head and common full-body silhouette, compared against July head-only reference and candidate03 full-body common-identity reference.
limits: Qualitative image comparison only; not metrology or dimensional validation.
No motion, collision, performance, material-color or rig assessment.
Not owner acceptance or final-art approval.
July reference controls head identity only; its body, perch and hanging wing train are excluded.
Candidate03 governs visible common full-body silhouette; perspective does not establish scale or hidden construction.

claims: July image is head identity only; body/perch/hanging wing train are excluded.
Candidate03 is the common visible full-body silhouette reference.

observations.finding: The head is recognizable, but the upper hook reads as a broad, mostly smooth and nearly uniform shell compared with the deeper convex, plated hook in the references. The lower jaw reads as a narrow rail/plate with an awkward termination rather than a substantial forked mandible framing a clear cheek opening. Optic appears inset and legible in these views; the remaining discrepancy is surrounding head mass/profile.
observations.evidence: Direct visual comparison of preserved head render with July head-only reference and candidate03 head.

observations.finding: The body reads as a tall, evenly armored egg or barrel, with a narrow upright segmented neck bridge. Candidate03 conveys a deeper breast and clearer taper toward pelvis; repeated similarly sized courses reinforce the cylindrical impression.
observations.evidence: Direct visual comparison of preserved three-quarter render with candidate03 common-body image.

observations.finding: The mantle reads as a rounded, separately attached shoulder pod with small, regular scales, rather than a swept compact wing cover integrated into the flank. This is an integration and shape-pattern mismatch; the render does show substantial coverage, so this review does not claim an area deficit.
observations.evidence: Direct visual comparison of preserved three-quarter render with candidate03 common-body image.

recommendations: Reshape the bill as a deeper convex hook with several larger swept structural plates, and broaden/articulate the cheek and lower jaw into a visible forked frame around the opening while retaining the current optic seating.

Integrate the folded mantle into the shoulder and flank as a longer tapered sweep with fewer, varied curved overlaps; in the same proportion pass, break up the uniform body courses and strengthen the breast-to-pelvis taper and curved neck connection.
